CausalChain: HCC tumor growth -> Hypoxic microenvironment -> Upregulation of HIF-1α -> Increased ENTPD2 expression on HCC cells -> Conversion of extracellular ATP to AMP -> Recruitment and accumulation of MDSCs -> Suppression of CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes -> Reduced efficacy of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors
Hypothesis: In HCC, inhibition of ENTPD2 will decrease MDSC-mediated immunosuppression and enhance the antitumor immune response when combined with PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint blockade, thereby overcoming resistance to immune-based therapies.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) represents a complex interplay between tumor cells and a highly immunosuppressive microenvironment in which factors such as hypoxia and metabolic alterations drive the accumulation of regulatory immune cells. Recent data indicate that hypoxia‐inducible factor‐1α (HIF‐1α) in HCC cells upregulates ectonucleoside triphosphate diphosphohydrolase 2 (ENTPD2), catalyzing the conversion of extracellular ATP into AMP. This metabolic shift may promote the recruitment and expansion of myeloid‐derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), which in turn dampen cytotoxic T cell activity and contribute to resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Here, we propose that targeted inhibition of ENTPD2 will reduce MDSC accumulation and thereby potentiate the efficacy of PD‐1/PD‐L1 blockade in HCC, offering a novel combinatorial strategy to overcome treatment resistance.
